newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed mart eagerly awaits prepay data.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed mart eagerly awaits prepay data.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities prices were firmer late this session in the wake of the Treasury's 10-year note auction as participants awaited Federal National Mortgage Associatio and Government National Mortgage Association July prepayment data due Thursday.
Late in the day, discount coupons were 5/32 to 6/32 firmer and premium coupons were up 3/32 to 4/32.
As reported the Treasury sold $12 billion of 10-year notes at an average yield of 6.205 percent. Traders cited lukewarm demand. An auction of $10 billion of 30-year bonds is scheduled for Thursday.

One New York interest only securities (IO) trader reported seeing several bid lists Wednesday. "The market has traded off for the past three days and today the market consolidated and moved back in the other direction," he said. This session, he noted, was the least hectic of this week.

"There were three or four large inverse bid lists. They all traded very well," he said, noting that some bonds which are trading at tight spreads are actually "very callable" -- meaning subject to prepayment risk.
"From the way the market is pricing these bonds, it looks like they are pricing in a giant prepayment surge," he said.
